messages:
Aisha: Hi all, Aisha here (platform eng). Fresh laptop (M1) and trying to get a minimal dev env up. Quick wins blocked: asdf install ruby 3.1.0 fails with "no acceptable C compiler" even though Xcode CLI is installed. Also my SSH key from 1Password isn't showing up when I try to clone private repos. Any pointers?

Riley: welcome! :wave: For the compiler error, run `xcode-select --install` and then `sudo xcodebuild -license accept` if you haven't. Sometimes Homebrew on M1 needs `arch -arm64 brew install gcc` for native compiles. What does `gcc --version` show?

Aisha: gcc 12.2.0 shows up. The ruby build still bails with: 

--- compile log ---
checking for clang... /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/clang
checking for sys/types.h... yes
checking for stdint.h... yes
checking for inttypes.h... yes
ld: library not found for -lssl
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
--- end ---

Sam: That ld error usually means Homebrew OpenSSL libs aren't on the search path. On M1 we use brew installed openssl@3 typically. Try: 

export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib/pkgconfig"
env RUBY_CONFIGURE_OPTS=\"--with-openssl-dir=$(brew --prefix openssl@3)\" asdf install ruby 3.1.0

If that still fails, try `HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_FILTERING=1` prefix.

Aisha: Ah thanks, will try. SSH key issue: I followed the onboarding doc which says `op item get onboarding/ssh --fields label=password` but op returns "not signed in" even after `op signin redwood`. 1Password CLI 2.x flow is confusing.

DevX-Bot: 1Password tips: run `eval $(op signin redwood --raw)` to persist session in your shell. If the onboarding entry is named differently, search `op item list | rg onboarding`. The bootstrap script also has a fallback: `curl -fsSL https://redwood-internal.dev/onboarding/fetch_ssh.sh | bash` (requires SSO).

Riley: I can add a temporary deploy key if needed. Also we often forget to add the SSH public key to GitHub after pulling from 1Password. Did you run `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_rsa` (macOS keychain) or `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`? Check `ssh -T git@github.com` for authentication.

Aisha: When I run `ssh -T git@github.com` I get "Permission denied (publickey)". I didn't see a public key in 1Password, only a private key item. How do folks usually store both?

Sam: We store the private key in 1P and the public key as a note on the same item. If your bootstrap script only pulls the private key, run `ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa > ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub` then add that pub key to your GitHub account (Settings -> SSH and GPG keys). Cam us if you need help.

Aisha: Thanks. Last thing: internal docs (https://redwood-internal.dev) 403s unless I'm on the VPN. Manager said infra needs to enable my VPN access. Who should I mention in the ticket?

infra-bot: Open a ticket in #help with subject "VPN request - new hire". Include: employee name, laptop serial, office (or "remote"), and which ip ranges you'll connect from if known. Tag @infra. SLA is usually same day during business hours. If you need temporary access now, ask your manager to approve emergency access and ping @infra in the ticket.

Aisha: Got it. Trying the openssl env flags next and will report back. Thanks for the quick help!
